stem: Mohan starts at point P facing North. He walks 20 km, turns right, walks 15 km, turns left, walks 5 km, turns right, walks 5 km, then turns right and walks 25 km to reach point Q. Point F is the midpoint of the straight line PQ. How far is F from Q, and in which direction does F lie from Q?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Reporting the direction of Q from F (East) instead of F from Q (West), reversing the reference point of the query.
Using |PQ|=20 as QF instead of half of it (10), giving 20 km West by failing to halve the distance for the midpoint.
Misidentifying the first left turn (from East) as South instead of North displaces Q off the x-axis, creating a diagonal PQ and a South-West direction for F from Q.

explanation: Track coordinates from P=(0,0): N 20->(0,20); right->East, E 15->(15,20); left->North, N 5->(15,25); right->East, E 5->(20,25); right->South, S 25->(20,0)=Q. All North segments (20+5=25) equal the South segment (25): they cancel. Net displacement: 20 East. |PQ|=20. F=midpoint=(10,0). From Q=(20,0): F=(10,0) is 10 km to the West.

explanation_sections.punchline: The hidden insight is that the scattered North legs (20+5=25) and the final South leg (25) cancel exactly, so PQ is purely East.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: build the coordinate path. Turn types: right from North=East, left from East=North, right from North=East, right from East=South. The last South leg spans all prior North movement. Net: (20,0). F=midpoint=(10,0). Direction of F from Q=(20,0): negative x-shift = West.
explanation_sections.lesson: In multi-leg paths, collect all same-axis components before computing displacement; then for a midpoint query, halve |PQ| and note the reversal when asking direction of start from end.
explanation_sections.timing: About 120-140 seconds. Two traps: (1) misidentifying left from East as South (gives wrong Q), and (2) reporting direction of Q from F instead of F from Q.
